### Indonesia

The full operational case. Inputs and outputs span 2001-2025 (on Zenodo, too large for the repo); validation is against 172 independent BMKG stations whose gauge record runs 2001-2021. Presented as curated figures and analysis.

:::

## Why two cases

The Bali bundle exists so anyone can run the whole pipeline and reproduce a result in minutes, without downloading anything. It is the proof that the toolchain works end to end.

The Indonesia study is what the framework was built for: a sparse-gauge tropical archipelago where a single global correction parameter would wash out real regional variability. It is also where the framework's honest limits show up most clearly (see [the correlation ceiling](indonesia.qmd#the-correlation-ceiling)).

Both cases use the same `src/` code and the same `config` structure. Swapping region is a matter of pointing the config at different inputs - see [Data Preparation](../tutorials/data-preparation.qmd) and [Configuration](../get-started/configuration.qmd).

::: {.callout-note}
The two cases are not directly comparable on headline numbers. Bali has 4 stations clustered in the south; Indonesia has 172 spread across the archipelago. The Bali figures are useful for checking the toolchain, not for drawing statistically reliable conclusions on their own.
:::
